answers.how: Calibrated motion using the white car’s known acceleration, then measured the yellow car’s depth-corrected displacement around 2.5 s.
Measured the curb-to-curb road span in perspective and converted the corresponding lane width using the acceleration-calibrated scale.
Measured the white car’s roof-to-wheel-bottom extent and corrected its pixel scale for depth.
Measured the white car’s longitudinal extent, correcting for perspective and its visible width.
Measured the yellow car’s length in the earlier, nearly side-on frames and applied the depth-corrected scale.
Measured the yellow car’s full vertical extent and converted it using its supplied depth.
Used the front-facing portion of the turn to measure transverse width, correcting for orientation and perspective.
Measured the visible bicycle wheels’ vertical diameters in later frames and corrected for depth.
Measured the traffic-light assembly from its ground base to its top, using the calibrated ground-plane perspective.
Converted the streetlights’ base-to-top pixel extents using their ground-plane positions; several lights give consistent heights.
Reconstructed the pedestrian’s ground positions at the beginning and end and divided the traveled distance by 2.958 s.
Measured head-to-foot height near both supplied pedestrian depths and averaged the converted measurements.
Tracked the bicycle across the sequence, corrected perspective using its supplied depths, and divided total travel by elapsed time.
